name: Schema-sync after migrations and split read-only/read-write container DB access
status_reason: Source review of supabase-schema-sync/execute.sh, both docker DB skill scripts, and migrations/001_add_agent_indexes.sql; no live database run, PostToolUse-hook trace, or role-provisioning evidence verified.; verified against sources 2026-09-14 (map author pass)
description: After a migration, supabase-schema-sync regenerates agent-facing schema docs under .claude/skills/db-query from information_schema; docker containers split DB access by Postgres user: readonly_user plus a write-verb denylist for queries, admin_user for migrations.
purpose: Schema knowledge stays current by regeneration, not manual editing: after a migration lands, supabase-schema-sync/execute.sh greps READONLY_DATABASE_URL (preferred, because introspection only reads and a narrowly scoped app DATABASE_URL would make the generated docs silently under-report the database) or DATABASE_URL out of the project .env - never sourcing the file - strips pgbouncer-incompatible params (pool_size, connection_limit, pgbouncer), and introspects information_schema for all non-system schemas (auth skipped unless --include-auth; the schema list is read with mapfile after a bug where read -ra truncated multi-line lists to one schema). For each schema it rewrites .claude/skills/db-query/schemas/<schema>.md with one markdown table per table: column, type, is_nullable, and the pg_description comment flattened to a single line with pipes escaped (comments are the carrier for known gotchas; the generated SKILL.md instructs authors to add COMMENT ON TABLE/COLUMN in the same migration that touches the column and then re-run the sync, since comment-only changes are zero blast radius). SKILL.md is rewritten every run as a lean index - table names only, no columns - with a Last synced timestamp, keeping context cost low, while the db-query execute.sh runner is written only if absent so local customizations survive re-syncs. Failure paths all exit 1 with named errors: missing .env, missing connection string, psql not installed, connection failure, or no schemas/tables surviving the filter; when the docs are stale or missing, the generated runner's --schema-doc mode errors with 'Run supabase-schema-sync to generate schema docs'. Container access is split by Postgres role, not by network: docker/skills/database-readonly/query.sh connects to cfn-postgres:5432/cfn_corporate as readonly_user with READONLY_DB_PASSWORD (default 'readonly_password') and pre-blocks writes with a case-insensitive denylist grep over the whole query string (INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|CREATE|ALTER|TRUNCATE), exiting 1 before psql runs; this is an application-level check only, and because it matches substrings a read query that merely names a column like created_at is also refused. docker/skills/database-readwrite/migrate.sh connects as admin_user with ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD (default 'admin_password'), accepts only up|down (anything else exits 1 with usage), and is an explicit placeholder: a TODO marks migration-tool integration pending, and today it only SELECTs the newest row from schema_migrations. migrations/001_add_agent_indexes.sql shows the raw-SQL shape that lands between those roles: idempotent CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on agents(team_id, status, spawned_at, two composites, completed_at) closed by a verification SELECT against pg_indexes.

sources.claim: Header contract: introspects the Supabase DB, reads DATABASE_URL from .env (never sources it), strips pgbouncer params, and writes a split structure to .claude/skills/db-query/: SKILL.md as a lean index (table names only, no columns), execute.sh written only if not present, and schemas/<schema>.md with full column details.

READONLY_DATABASE_URL wins where a project defines one, with the rationale inline: introspection only ever reads, and a project's DATABASE_URL may be a narrowly scoped app role that cannot see most schemas, which would make the generated docs silently under-report the database; falls back to DATABASE_URL; surrounding quotes stripped; missing .env, missing URL, or missing psql each exit 1.

Schema auto-detection lists information_schema.schemata excluding pg_catalog, information_schema, pg_toast and temp schemas; the auth schema is filtered out unless --include-auth; connection failure or an empty result exits 1, and mapfile replaced read -ra because read consumed only the first line of multi-line schema lists, truncating the set to one schema.

Per-schema docs are built from information_schema.columns LEFT JOINed to pg_description with \\x01 as delimiter (comment text may contain pipes), the comment flattened to one line via regexp_replace so a multi-paragraph COMMENT ON COLUMN cannot break the markdown table row, plus a table-level comment from obj_description; each schemas/<schema>.md is regenerated wholesale on every run.

The generated SKILL.md carries the freshness protocol: do not guess table or column names, treat a non-empty pg_description comment as a documented landmine, add COMMENT ON TABLE/COLUMN in the same migration that touches a column and then re-run supabase-schema-sync to refresh the docs (comment-only changes are zero blast radius), plus a Last synced timestamp; the run summary reports each output file with a bytes/4 token estimate.

The db-query execute.sh runner is emitted from a heredoc only when it does not already exist ('already exists, preserved'), so re-syncs overwrite SKILL.md and schemas/ but never clobber a customized runner; the embedded runner's --schema-doc mode errors with 'Run supabase-schema-sync to generate schema docs' when the schema file is missing, and its --sql mode re-greps DATABASE_URL from .env, re-strips pgbouncer params, and prefixes SET search_path when --schema is given.

Read-only container path: connects with psql to POSTGRES_HOST (default cfn-postgres):5432, database POSTGRES_DB (default cfn_corporate), as fixed user readonly_user with READONLY_DB_PASSWORD (default 'readonly_password'); query is a required first argument.

Write prevention is an application-level denylist: the whole query string is grepped case-insensitively for INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|DROP|CREATE|ALTER|TRUNCATE and any match exits 1 with 'Write operations are not allowed with read-only access' before psql runs; because it is substring matching over the raw text, a read-only query merely containing a token like created_at or 'update' in a string literal is also refused, and it is not evidence of a DB-enforced permission on readonly_user.

Read-write container path: same host/port/database defaults but connects as admin_user with ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD (default 'admin_password'); takes direction up (default) or down, any other argument exits 1 with usage.

The read-write path is a declared placeholder: a TODO says to integrate a migration tool (node-pg-migrate, Flyway, Liquibase) and 'Migration placeholder - integrate with migration tool in Phase 2'; today the script only SELECTs the newest version from schema_migrations, so no migration SQL is actually applied by it.

The migration file itself is hand-run idempotent SQL: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS on agents(team_id), (status), (spawned_at), composites (team_id,status), (status,spawned_at), (team_id,spawned_at,status), and (completed_at), closed by a verification SELECT of indexname/indexdef from pg_indexes for public.agents; it neither inserts into schema_migrations nor is invoked by migrate.sh.

unknowns: What triggers the sync in practice: repo-level config (a PostToolUse hook said to auto-run supabase-schema-sync after detected migration-apply commands) lives outside the four scoped files and was not evidenced here; from the scoped sources alone the sync is a manually invoked script.

Where readonly_user and admin_user are provisioned (init SQL, compose env, or GRANT statements) and whether Postgres itself restricts readonly_user to SELECT is unverified; the denylist in query.sh is the only access control visible in scope.
Whether the schema_migrations table queried by migrate.sh exists anywhere in this repo, and who creates or writes it, was not checked; migrations/001 does not reference it.
How the docker skills are mounted or invoked inside containers (compose wiring, network aliases beyond the cfn-postgres default) is outside the scoped files and untraced.
Whether any migration numbering beyond 001 exists, and whether migrations are applied by hand via psql or by an external tool, is not determinable from the single scoped migration file.
